newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower on position squaring ahead of the expiry of next week of the October contract. October shed $2.80 to close at $348.00 per tonne while December eased $1.40 to close at $346.00. Traders said that supplies of Brazilian sugar are abundant which may depress prices. Trading was dominated by traders rolling long positions from October to March, pressuring the near month. However, there was some scale-down buying below 12.00 cents/lb providing support.

RUSSIA - The fifth Russian sugar beet test does not signal any improvement in crop prospects. The increase in the beet weight per ha was 19 per cent below that of last year and 43 per cent below average. The beet weight per ha at the beginning of September reached 21.78 tonnes, down from 25.70 tonnes last year and the average of 27.15 tonnes. The increase in sugar content was slightly higher than last year (+1.2 vs 0.9 per cent). However, the sugar yield per ha at the beginning of September reached only 3.11 tonnes, white value, nearly 14 per cent less than last year and 16 per cent below average. These figures confirm that Russian beet sugar production will fall below last year's 2.228 million tonnes in raw value terms.

AUSTRIA - After the slump in 1994/95, Australian sugar consumption is well on course for the highest level in five years. Sugar offtake in July 1996 amounted to 39,803 tonnes, raw value, up from 37,410 tonnes in July 1995. This brought cumulative consumption in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 343,248 tonnes, up from last year's 314,475 tonnes. Total consumption in 1994/95 amounted to 384,050 tonnes, down from 416,742 tonnes in 1993/94. Sugar exports in July 1996 reached 4,250 tonnes, up from 3,823 tonnes in July 1995. This brought cumulative exports in the first ten months of 1995/96 up to 45,418 tonnes against 25,538 tonnes in 1994/95. Total exports in 1994/95 reached 31,276 tonnes, sharply down from 100,560 tonnes exported in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Romania with 30,450 tonnes whites against 3,766 tonnes and Croatia with 2,408 tonnes against 550 tonnes.

JAPAN - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 121,662 tonnes, raw value, down from 130,141 tonnes imported in the like month the previous year. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 1.39 million tonnes compared to 1.38 million tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.72 million tonnes compared to 1.70 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/July 1995/96 were Thailand with 659,371 tonnes raws against 489,577 tonnes, Australia with 484,626 tonnes compared to 573,398 tonnes and South Africa with 148,241 tonnes against 56,922 tonnes. Sugar exports in October/July 1995/96 continued to be negligible (3,013 tonnes vs 1,130 tonnes).

DENMARK - The latest beet test results of September 2 continued to be rather unsatisfactory. Beet yield per ha amounted to no more than 39.3 tonnes, down from 40.8 tonnes in 1995 and significantly below the five-year average (1991/95) of 45.0 tonnes. Sugar content on September 2 amounted to 15.7 per cent against 16.0 per cent in 1995 and the average of 15.4 per cent. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 6.18 tonnes per ha, white value, more than 5 per cent below last year's 6.52 tonnes and 10.7 per cent down on the average of 6.92 tonnes. Despite these rather disenchanting results, industry sources expect sugar production to be around last year's levels of 470,000 tonnes, raw value.

The Egyptian company Multitrade bought 60,000 tonnes of raw sugar, half of the amount from Louis Dreyfus. Price and other details were not immediately available but traders said delivery was believed to be between July and September 1997.
